messages.author: 83b63066408210ec
messages.subject: Extraneous parametres worsen convergence
parts:
I was trying to run a certain multilevel model and I wanted to compare the results of using one, two, or three levels in the model. For that, I added a data variable called n_levels and, in the model, added if/elses that change the model depending on whether n_levels = 1, 2, or 3. However, when n_levels = 1 or 2, convergence of the actually used parametres is terrible, often with Rhat > 40. After fiddling with it, I found out that the mere fact of adding extraneous parametres (without using them for anything) seems to worsen convergence considerably.

Why does it happen? Is it avoidable?

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: Extraneous parametres worsen convergence
parts:
Extra parameters are always bad - but from my experience they don't hurt so much IF you assign a prior to it (preferably a N(0,1) if your stuff is on the unit-scale as it should be).

Sebastian

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Extraneous parametres worsen convergence
parts:
On Thursday, January 5, 2017 at 12:42:46 PM UTC-5, Pedro Carvalho wrote:
These parametres are all strictly positive; is there an equivalent thing to the unit-scale for those? And why do extra parametres affect convergence for parametres they're not connected to?
Because it it is trying to draw from a joint posterior distribution and any parameters that are unused and do not have proper priors make the joint posterior distribution improper.

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Extraneous parametres worsen convergence
parts: And it will screw up warm-up, no? Optimizing sampler params when one or several parameters has nothing to optimize against (it's disconnected from the shape of posterior, so the simulated particle can go in any direction without any change in the hamiltonian). The warm-up would adapt to a parameter that shouldn't be adapted to, but that can screw up the sampling of all other parameters. p(unused | D, other params) \sim constant; warmup would adapt to something that makes no sense and cause divergences during sampling, no?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Extraneous parametres worsen convergence
parts:
If there's an unused (independent) parameter with a unit
normal, then no adaptation is necessary---the unit starting point is
correct. So that should be relatively stable compared to the
harder parts of the warmup.

- Bob
